gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Wide channels run into every counter of Noto Sans Thaana, giving its big lowercase forms an approachable ease. But Origami's single-stroke brush lines hold one constant width, a drawn-string steadiness that gives the headings a poured-lead mass.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-thai: Origami draws dowel-like stems and bent-dowel arcs, a sign-painter's brush look with a contemporary edge. Noto Sans Thai swells its lowercase like glass beads and leaves the round letters open, which keeps extended reading approachable and smooth.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-thai-loo: Noto Sans Thai Looped stands tall, its lowercase bodies looking bold. What stands out most is the shift from Origami's uniform brush line, with no thinning anywhere, to that tall, spacious sans-serif body.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-numans: Origami paints with a ballpoint's pressure-free line, one constant width throughout. Numans, a sans-serif with far-hanging s ends and wide tracking, gives those plain strokes a spaced-out, swollen lowercase to sit against.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-orienta: Orienta keeps its counters breathing like a cut reed, with little height gap between cases. And over a full column the plain sans text moves along quietly, while Origami's round-tip marker line stays blunt up top.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-parkinsans: Origami excels at poured-lead mass in a constant-width brush line. Parkinsans, a sans-serif with wide-mouthed letters and one stroke thickness, is the one that stays crisp when shrunk, its lowercase rising close to capitals.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-questrial: A sign-painter's single-stroke brush line at constant width gives Origami its poured-lead lowercase mass. Questrial, the sans below, does the quieter job with its flat, stencil-cut strokes and a tall band of letters.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-radio-canada: A single-stroke brush line at constant width defines Origami. Both keep a steady line with no pressure variation, which is what ties Radio Canada's plain sans text to the heading.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-readex-pro: Single-stroke and sign-painted, Origami sets its lowercase in a mass like poured lead type. And Readex Pro, a sans with broad gaps at the terminals, holds an unvarying weight so paragraphs glide.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-roboto: Roboto gives its round letters generous mouths and a low capital-to-body contrast. Beneath Origami's constant-width brush strokes, which have no thin lines to vanish in glare, that sans-serif body stays out of the way.
